name: GEO600 — dark matter searches
summary: An independent dark-matter analysis of the German–British gravitational-wave interferometer, using the beam-splitter material's response to scalar dark matter.
detection_principle: An ultralight scalar field changes the electron mass or electromagnetic constants, modulating the beam splitter's size and refractive index and leaving a narrowband signal in the arm phase difference.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2021 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Direct limits for scalar field dark matter from a gravitational-wave detector

key_parameters.name: Analysis data
key_parameters.value: Seven segments of approximately 10⁵ s each in 2016 and 2019

results.summary: No credible dark-matter signal; model-dependent scalar-coupling limits were obtained.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
